finalText:
**Found it and fixed it.**

`engine.js` rounded the running total to 2 decimal places after the percent coupon, and again after the flat coupon, before converting to the order's currency. That's an extra rounding step the math doesn't need.

A flat coupon never showed the bug, since subtracting a whole dollar amount from a 2-decimal total stays clean. But a percent coupon (like 10% off) creates more decimal places, so rounding early threw away real cents before the currency conversion multiplied everything back up. That's why it only broke when a percent coupon stacked with non-USD currencies (GBP, CAD, JPY) — GBP and CAD failed on every percent case, JPY only on the basket that happened to land on an ugly fraction.

The fix: carry full precision through both coupon steps and round only once, at the very end, after conversion.

All 40 tests pass now, up from 30/40, in about 0.1s.
